classification.difficultyReason: Substitute the stated value and apply the taught order of operations, including brackets and fraction numerators.

questions.mappingNote: Every part replaces x with 2 and evaluates the resulting numerical expression. Neither supplied reuse candidate matches this complete eight-part task.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 substitutes the given value, then evaluates in successive equality rows. Examples 2 and 3 reinforce substitution and the order of operations.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute one positive integer and evaluate using brackets, multiplication and division.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute one negative integer and evaluate simple sums, products, quotients and bracketed expressions.

questions.mappingNote: Every part substitutes x=-6 into a numerical expression; negative-number substitution is the directly assessed skill. Neither supplied reuse candidate matches this whole eight-part task.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 defines substitution and Example 1 substitutes values directly, brackets a negative substituted value in multiplication, and evaluates in successive equalities. Page 3 reinforces substitution and the order of operations in Examples 2 and 3. Evaluate brackets or the fraction numerator before the remaining multiplication or division.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute one negative integer and evaluate simple sums, products, quotients and bracketed expressions.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute a negative integer while distinguishing powers of a negative quantity, an external minus sign and a coefficient outside a power.

questions.mappingNote: All seven expressions require substitution of n=-3. Parts b, c and e distinguish the scope of the negative sign; parts f and g distinguish squaring the product from multiplying the square. Neither supplied reuse candidate has this complete stem and set of seven expressions.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 introduces substitution and power notation. Page 3 Example 3 substitutes into powers, distinguishes (-m)^2 from -m^2, expands a negative cube as repeated multiplication and evaluates the bracketed product before squaring.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute a negative integer while distinguishing powers of a negative quantity, an external minus sign and a coefficient outside a power.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute signed values while respecting negative bases, power scope and the distinction between a powered variable and a powered product.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts use a=-2, b=5 and c=-1. Substitution of negative values is the primary assessed skill; powers in b, d, e, g and j–l require correct sign and bracket scope. Neither supplied reuse candidate matches this complete task.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 substitutes signed values explicitly. Example 2 substitutes multiple pronumerals and evaluates powers before addition or subtraction. Example 3 distinguishes powers of a variable from powers of a bracketed product and evaluates negative bases in brackets.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute negative values into sums, differences, powers, products and quotients, preserving the scope of powers.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute negative integers and a negative fraction, evaluating squares before subtraction.

questions.mappingNote: All four parts require substitution using the stated values. Parts a and b additionally require squaring a negative fraction. Neither supplied reuse candidate matches this complete four-part task and its givens.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 substitutes negative values using brackets. Example 2 substitutes a fraction, squares bracketed values and expresses fractional results as mixed numbers. Example 3 distinguishes a squared negative value from a negative square.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute negative integers and a negative fraction, evaluating squares before subtraction.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute two negative values into expressions involving products, quotients, sums and powers.

questions.mappingNote: Every part requires substitution of x=-2 and y=-1. Parts f, j and k additionally require evaluating powers before multiplication or addition. The complete task differs from both supplied reuse candidates, so it is authored independently.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 substitutes negative numbers in brackets and evaluates products before addition. Example 2 substitutes two pronumerals and evaluates their powers separately. Example 3 distinguishes a power of a negative value from an external minus sign and evaluates squares and cubes.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute two negative values into expressions involving products, quotients, sums and powers.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute three values, including a negative value, and distinguish powers of a product from a negative sign outside a power.

questions.mappingNote: Question 7 combines three-pronumeral substitution with negative values and powers. Parts e, h and i particularly require attention to the scope of brackets and indices. Neither supplied reuse candidate matches the complete task, givens and nine expressions.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 substitutes numerical values, brackets negative values and evaluates. Example 2 substitutes several pronumerals and evaluates powers before addition or subtraction. Example 3 distinguishes a power of a bracketed negative quantity from a negative sign outside a power.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute three values, including a negative value, and distinguish powers of a product from a negative sign outside a power.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose and sequence inverse operations for two-step equations, then substitute each result into the original equation to verify it.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–c use one inverse operation. Parts d–f and i isolate a multiple before dividing. Parts g–h multiply both sides by the denominator before dividing by the coefficient. Every part explicitly requires a substitution check.
questions.methodNote: Apply the same inverse operation to both sides, isolate the pronumeral, retain exact fractions and check by substituting into the original left-hand side. Example 4 demonstrates each required equation form; page 7 confirms that operation boxes may be omitted.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Routine one-step and two-step equations with positive coefficients, followed by substitution checks.

classification.difficultyReason: Isolate the variable term, handle negative coefficients or division, and verify the solution by signed substitution.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–c follow Example 5a, d–f follow Example 5b with negative coefficients, and g–i follow Example 5c with fractional variable terms. The explicit checking instruction also assesses verification by substitution.
questions.methodNote: Use equivalent equations and the inverse operations in Example 5: isolate the variable term, then divide by its coefficient or multiply by its denominator. Check by substitution as demonstrated in Example 4.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Two-step equations include negative coefficients and fractional variable terms, with substitution checks required.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply additive inverses and recognise that isolating -m requires reversing its sign to obtain m.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–d, f–g and i require one additive inverse operation. Parts e and h additionally require interpreting the coefficient of -m as -1, making the negative-coefficient skill the most advanced assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Use equivalent equations by adding or subtracting the same number on both sides. For parts e and h, isolate -m and divide both sides by -1, following the negative-coefficient method in Example 5b.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Solve additive equations with signed numbers, including two equations containing a negative coefficient of m.

classification.difficultyReason: Divide both sides by the displayed coefficient, applying signed division and simplifying exact quotients.

questions.mappingNote: Every part requires division by its numerical coefficient. Parts b, c, d and h directly assess negative coefficients, making that the closest primary skill; the remaining parts assess ordinary one-step equations.
questions.methodNote: Equivalent equations permit division of both sides by the same non-zero number. Example 4b divides by the coefficient and expresses an exact answer as a mixed number; Example 5b includes division by a negative coefficient. Page 7 explicitly removes the operation boxes from subsequent solutions.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: One inverse operation isolates the pronumeral; several coefficients are negative and several answers are exact fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Each equation requires multiplication by a positive denominator, followed by a substitution check; some solutions are negative.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly assess a single inverse multiplication, including negative numerical results, and explicitly require substitution checks. None of the supplied reuse candidates matches this complete six-part task.
questions.methodNote: Equivalent equations preserve solutions when both sides are multiplied by the same non-zero number. Example 5c demonstrates undoing division by multiplying by the denominator. Example 4 demonstrates checking by substituting the solution and showing LHS = RHS.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Each equation requires multiplication by a positive denominator, followed by a substitution check; some solutions are negative.

classification.difficultyReason: Two inverse operations, including division by negative coefficients and exact fractional solutions, followed by substitution checks.

questions.mappingNote: Example 4c supports a–d, h and i; Example 5b supports negative coefficients in e–g. Example 4b–d supports mixed-number answers and substitution checks. Negative-coefficient equations are the most advanced directly assessed type.
questions.methodNote: Maintain equivalent equations by applying the same inverse operation to both sides. Isolate the variable term, divide by its coefficient, retain exact fractional values, then substitute into the original equation to check LHS = RHS.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Two inverse operations, including division by negative coefficients and exact fractional solutions, followed by substitution checks.

classification.difficultyReason: Combines one-step and two-step equations, including fractional variable terms and an exact fractional solution.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a and b require one inverse operation. Parts c and d isolate a multiple of the variable before division. Part e follows Example 4d by multiplying by 4 then dividing by 5. Part f follows Example 5c by isolating the fractional variable term then multiplying by 7. None of the supplied reuse candidates matches this complete six-part task.
questions.methodNote: Apply the same inverse operation to both sides to obtain equivalent equations. Example 4 models addition, division and multiplication by a denominator; Example 5 models isolating a variable term before dividing or multiplying.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combines one-step and two-step equations, including fractional variable terms and an exact fractional solution.

classification.difficultyReason: Translate the stated operation sequence into an equation using the supplied pronumeral, then undo its operations in reverse order.

questions.mappingNote: Part a translates addition and subtracts 5; b and c translate multiplication and divide by the coefficient; d subtracts 3 before dividing by 5; e reverses division by multiplying by 6; f adds 5 before multiplying by 3. Each uses the named pronumeral in its description. The offered reuse question is not source-identical: its pronumerals, part count and later tasks differ, so this complete question is authored normally.
questions.methodNote: Page 5 establishes equivalent equations through equal operations on both sides. Example 4 on page 6 demonstrates inverse operations and exact mixed-number results. Examples 5 and 6 on page 7 demonstrate undoing operations in reverse order and translating verbal descriptions into equations.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Translate explicit arithmetic descriptions into one-step or two-step equations and solve by inverse operations, retaining exact fractional results.

classification.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate inverse-operation sequence for additive and fractional coefficient equations using the demonstrated forms.

questions.mappingNote: Part a follows Example 4a by subtracting 5. Parts d and e follow Example 4d by multiplying by the denominator and then dividing by the coefficient. The question region on page 9 remains within Exercise 6B, above the 6C topic band.
questions.methodNote: Page 5 establishes equivalent equations using the same operation on both sides. previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply one or two inverse operations, retaining exact negative and fractional solutions.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a and e translate subtraction from a constant and solve a negative unit coefficient. previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Translate operation order accurately, including subtraction from a constant, and solve equations with negative coefficients or fractional terms.

classification.difficultyReason: Compare the pronumerals and their powers in pairs of terms, including multivariable terms.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare the pronumerals and their powers in pairs of terms, including multivariable terms.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify separated like terms, carry their signs when grouping coefficients, and retain unlike terms unchanged.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–n collect coefficients of one pronumeral; o–p collect two adjacent groups; q–v rearrange separated like terms and retain unlike terms. Every part directly assesses collect-like-terms. The supplied reuse candidates have different complete tasks and cannot be reused.
questions.methodNote: Page 12 explains that like terms have identical pronumerals and powers and combines their coefficients using distribution. Example 11 on page 13 adds or subtracts coefficients, first rearranging separated like terms when needed.
